text:
maya: Quick check — running into flaky streaming in RN WebView when we rotate ephemeral tokens. Browser works fine, but the RN WebView stream drops after token refresh. Anyone seen this? :thinking:
liam: seen similar with the old auth flow. Are you doing token swap via postMessage from RN -> webview or using a refresh endpoint inside the webview itself?
maya: postMessage from native to webview to set `window.__RW_TOKEN`. Then the JS client swaps Authorization header and reconnects. In logs I see 401 then reconnect, but payloads stop arriving (no error).
adarsh: two quick suspects: CORS preflight + exposed headers, or the streaming connection reuses a stale TCP/HTTP2 connection that the server rejects silently. In browser the fetch reconnect is cleaner. RN WebView sometimes keeps sockets alive.
maya: hmm that matches — I added `Authorization` header on reconnect but stream still silent. Any headers we should expose?
liam: make sure server sends `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Connection,Upgrade` isn't enough. For token rotation you should send a short-lived session cookie OR explicitly close old stream on the server side when new token is issued. Another fix: force a full new connection (change query param like `?v=${Date.now()}`) so RN doesn't reuse.
sara: also check the JS SDK's retry/backoff. We had a bug where `stream.cancel()` didn't fully tear down websocket fallback; on reconnect it thought it was still open and dropped messages. Which SDK version?
maya: using `@redwood/sdk-js@1.2.0` (installed via CDN in the webview).
adarsh: try this quick repro change in webview client (adds random suffix so connection is new):
```js
const url = `https://inference.redwood.com/v1/stream?client=${Date.now()}`;
const s = new EventSource(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
```
If that fixes, it's RN connection reuse. If not, paste logs.
liam: also check console for CORS error lines — RN WebView sometimes hides them. Use `window.onerror` to forward console to native for debugging.
maya: good idea, will enable. If it's a server close on rotate, what's the best pattern for ephemeral tokens? We want short lived tokens for security but avoid client churn.
sara: pattern we use in mobile wrappers: keep a native refresh flow (native gets new token and injects it into JS before reconnect). And server accepts both the old and new token for a 2s window and emits a `session:rotated` event so client can gracefully reconnect. That saved us from silent drops.
adarsh: alternative: use a long-lived websocket token and refresh user auth separately for API calls. Depends on threat model.
maya: thanks. One more — code review ping: I pushed a tiny change to `rn-webview-wrapper` to add `?v=` suffix and a test, could someone look? PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rn-webview-wrapper/pull/312 :eyes:
liam: I'll take a look in ~30m.
sara: I can review after lunch, leaving small comments on error handling if needed.
devex-bot: Documentation note: see internal doc on mobile token patterns — https://docs.redwood.internal/mobile-auth#ephemeral-tokens (added by devex-bot) :book:
maya: perfect — milestone-wise, if the `?v=` hack works I can ship a quick patch and then follow up with server-side rotation window. Thanks all :thumbsup:
